summary.intent: Execute Phase 20 (vault-migration) end-to-end: implement vault blob v2 binary format across core, API, Rust desktop, and web client, then verify the migration works correctly.
summary.outcome: All 4 plans executed successfully. Migration was confirmed working (DB shows migrated_at timestamp). Several bugs discovered and fixed during UAT: v2 blob parsing in folder sync, recovery tool IPNS resolution chain, and security issues (key bounds checking, debug redaction).

repo: The vault migration for myankelev@gmail.com succeeded silently — NestJS doesn't auto-log incoming requests, so POST /vault/migrate was invisible in server logs even when it succeeded.
fetchAndDecryptMetadata in both folder.service.ts and sdk-core blindly JSON.parse'd IPFS blob bytes — it did not account for v2 binary format, causing sync failures after migration.
The IPNS controller at apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.controller.ts requires JWT auth on all endpoints — recovery tool cannot use it without credentials.
Kubo at 192.168.133.114:5001 resolves IPNS via /api/v0/name/resolve but does not send CORS headers, blocking browser requests.

Kubo gateway at 192.168.133.114:8080 serves /ipns/{name} paths directly, returns X-Ipfs-Roots header with CID, and allows all CORS origins — this is the correct approach for browser-based IPNS resolution.
Subfolder IPNS records are only in the CipherBox API DB cache and are not propagated to the public DHT, so the recovery tool cannot resolve them without API access.

orval generates { [key: string]: unknown } | null instead of string | null for nullable string fields — the as unknown as string casts in useAuth.ts are the correct workaround for this pre-existing orval codegen bug.
The desktop vault init was double-wrapping rootFolderKey with ECIES — once for DB storage and once for v2 blob — using the same public key.

code.finding: fetchAndDecryptMetadata blindly JSON.parsed IPFS blob bytes without checking for v2 binary format header — fixed to detect and strip v2 header before parsing.
Same v2 blob parsing bug as folder.service.ts — SDK version also needed v2 detection before JSON.parse.
Migration IIFE: deriveVaultIpnsKeypair() was called twice with identical inputs in PATH A. Hoisted to single call. Also had redundant destructure/re-wrap of ipnsKeypair.
serialize_vault_blob_v2 was changed to return Result to support key length bounds checking — callers needed ? propagation added.
InitVaultRequest and VaultResponse derived Debug — custom Debug impls added to redact encrypted key material from logs.

fetchFromIpfs could return undefined on non-200/non-404 responses, causing detectBlobVersion to crash on undefined.length. IPNS resolution went through multiple broken fallback chains before being simplified to a single /ipns/{name} HEAD request on the IPFS gateway using X-Ipfs-Roots header.

workflow: NestJS does not auto-log HTTP requests by default — absence of log lines does not mean the endpoint was never called.
When debugging 'silent failures', check the database directly before assuming the operation failed.
The gsd:debug workflow with Playwright console inspection is effective for diagnosing frontend issues that don't surface in server logs.
Security review (security:review command) running in parallel with UAT checkpoint is an efficient pattern — issues found and fixed before verification completed.
The simplify workflow caught a real double-ECIES-wrap bug in the desktop vault init that would have caused incorrect behavior.
Kubo's /ipns/{name} gateway path is the correct approach for browser-based IPNS resolution in local dev — avoids CORS issues that affect the API port.

friction: Phase directory was in cipher-box-phase-20 instead of cipher-box — init tool failed initially, requiring manual directory discovery.
NestJS silent request logging caused a lengthy debug investigation that concluded the migration had actually succeeded all along.
IPNS records for subfolders are only in the API DB cache and not propagated to the DHT — recovery tool hit a dead end on subfolder resolution.
orval codegen generates incorrect types for nullable string fields — requires as unknown as string casts throughout useAuth.ts.
Kubo API port lacks CORS headers, blocking all browser-direct API calls for IPNS resolution.
Recovery tool IPNS resolution required multiple iteration cycles (delegated routing → Kubo API → CipherBox API → gateway /ipns/ path) before finding a working approach.
The checkpoint was held open for an extended UAT session while debugging the migration, security review, simplify review, and recovery tool fixes were all completed.
open_items: M-1: Recovery tool private key not zeroed after use in memory.
M-2: No dedup guard on concurrent migration from multiple browser tabs — race condition possible.
M-3: ECIES re-wrap on every root folder FUSE publish — optimization requires caching wrapped key in AppState.
L-1: Zero-length key accepted by v2 blob deserializers.
L-2: No SRI hashes on CDN scripts in recovery.html.
Recovery tool cannot recover subfolder contents when IPNS records are only in the API DB cache and not propagated to the DHT — architectural limitation.
Device registry sync failing with CryptoError: Invalid registry format (todo captured: fix-device-registry-cryptoerror-invalid-registry-format).
Bin IPNS name 404 resolution failure during sync (todo captured: fix-bin-ipns-name-404-resolution-failure).
Kubo IPNS records for subfolders should be published to the DHT so the recovery tool can resolve them without API access.
